target: राजेश हर साल अपने जन्मदिन पर दोस्तों को बुलाता है।
english: Rajesh invites his friends over on his birthday every year.
reason: Textbook-virtue filler (plants a tree every birthday) — a moral-lesson sentence, not something a learner will ever say. Same habitual-present pattern with an ordinary birthday situation.

target: यह रास्ता उस रास्ते से छोटा है।
english: This route is shorter than that one.
reason: Pointless trivia (stone vs brick). Keeps the से comparative but in a sentence people actually use when getting around.

target: हमारी मीटिंग लंच से पहले होती है।
reason: Niche cultural trivia (Ramlila before Dussehra) — no everyday use. Same 'X से पहले होती है' pattern applied to a normal schedule.

target: मैंने कल बाज़ार से नया फ़ोन ख़रीदा।
english: I bought a new phone from the market yesterday.
reason: Decorative occupational card (goldsmith making a gold necklace) — same stratum as potter/cobbler cards. Replaced with an everyday ने-perfective sentence.

target: वह अपने माता-पिता के साथ रहता है।
reason: Preachy/moralising ('respects everything his parents say'). Keeps अपने + माता-पिता in a plain factual sentence learners actually need.

target: मैंने अपना काम पूरा कर लिया है।
reason: Padded and oddly boastful ('twenty-seven countries so far'); nobody says this. Same अपना + present-perfect structure in a genuinely useful sentence.

target: क्रिकेट खेलते हुए मेरा घुटना छिल गया।
english: I scraped my knee while playing cricket.
reason: Niche trivia (pitthu garam) and the English drops the subject entirely. Same 'खेलते हुए' pattern with a common activity and a proper subject.

target: यह बैग उस बैग के मुक़ाबले हल्का है।
english: This bag is lighter compared to that one.
reason: Trivia (silver vs gold weight) that no learner will use. Keeps the के मुक़ाबले comparative in an everyday shopping/packing context.

target: अनिल सीढ़ियों से नीचे गिर पड़ा।
reason: 'ग़लती से गिर पड़ा' is translationese — falling isn't something done by mistake in Hindi phrasing. Keeps the गिर पड़ा compound verb, said the natural way.

target: जो लड़का वहाँ खड़ा है, वह मेरा भाई है।
english: The boy standing over there is my brother.
reason: Preachy motto ('a student who works hard succeeds'). Same जो...वह relative-clause structure in an ordinary spoken sentence.

target: जब प्रिया छोटी थी, तब वह बहुत ज़िद्दी थी।
english: When Priya was little, she was very stubborn.
reason: English says 'Riya' but the Hindi says प्रिया — mismatched card; also the third verbatim copy of the same template. Rewritten with the full जब...तब correlative and different vocabulary.
